J U D G M E N T
PER HON’BLE MR. VIRENDER BHAT, JUDICIAL MEMBER
1. The appellant, a consumer of electricity in the State of Uttar Pradesh,
has filed this appeal against the order dated 18.08.2021 passed by the 4th
respondent Uttar Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission (hereinafter
referred to as “the Commission”) thereby rejecting the claim of the appellant
for compensation under Section 57 of the Electricity Act, 2003.
____________________________________________________________________________________
Appeal No.299 of 2021 Page 2 of 17

2. The facts of the case lie within very narrow compass and emerge
undisputed between the parties.
3. The appellant had been availing supply of electricity from the 2nd
respondent i.e. the distribution licensee for agricultural purposes. The
electricity connection had been taken by the appellant for running a private
tubewell. It appears that the Executive Engineer of the 2nd respondent
carried out an inspection on 25.11.2018 and found certain facts which,
purportedly, made out prima facie case of theft of electricity from the said
connection. The electricity supply was disconnected on the same date. The
First Information Report (FIR) regarding these facts was lodged with the
concerned Police Station on 27.11.2018, clearly beyond the stipulated period
of 24 hours as envisaged under clause 8.1 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity
Supply Code, 2005. However, neither a police report nor a criminal
complaint has been filed before the competent special court dealing with the
offences under the Electricity Act, 2003, till date in pursuance to the
inspection carried out in the wake of said FIR.
4. Final assessment order came to be issued by 3rd respondent on
09.04.2019 under Section 126 of the Electricity Act, 2003.
5. The appellant filed a petition bearing no.1497/2019 before the
Commission under Section 57 of the Electricity Act, 2003, read with clause
____________________________________________________________________________________
Appeal No.299 of 2021 Page 3 of 17

8.2 of Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005, seeking directions for
immediate restoration of electricity supply as well as action against
respondents for gross violation of the provisions of the Code which included
payment of compensation to the appellant. The petition was dismissed by
the Commission vide order dated 16.03.2020 on the ground of
maintainability in view of certain legal remedies which had been pursued by
the appellant before approaching the Commission with the petition. The
appellant assailed the said order dated 16.03.2020 of the Commission
before this Tribunal by way of appeal no.140/2020 which was allowed vide
judgment dated 22.12.2020 thereby reviving the proceedings of the petition
before the Commission with the direction to the Commission to consider and
adjudicate the same on merits in accordance with law.
6. Accordingly, the Commission revived the petition no.1497/2019 and
held fresh proceedings w.e.f. 11.01.2021. In the order dated 27.04.2021,
the Commission recorded the agreement of the parties to the effect that
appellant shall make payment of the final assessment as per the statement
to be prepared by the respondent. The Commission also directed the
Executive Engineer to restore the connection of the appellant within 24 hours
after the said payment was settled by the appellant. As recorded in the
impugned order of the Commission, the appellant made a payment of
____________________________________________________________________________________
Appeal No.299 of 2021 Page 4 of 17

Rs.42,896/- after adjusting the amount of monthly bills that had already been
paid by him.
7. Finally, the Commission held the appellant not entitled to the
compensation under Section 57 of the Electricity Act, 2003, on the ground
that the appellant was in arrears on account of final assessment and as such
no compensation could be awarded in view of Regulation 8.1 of UPERC
(Standards of Performance) Regulations, 2019. However, the Commission
found the conduct of the distribution licensee in not lodging an FIR within 24
hours of the detection of the theft and in failure to file a case before the
special court within 30 days of disconnection of electricity to the appellant’s
premises as an act of non-compliance of the provisions of the Electricity Act,
Rules and the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and decided to initiate separate
suo-motu proceedings in this regard. The relevant portion of the impugned
order of the Commission is extracted hereinbelow: -
“6. The Commission is of the view that APTEL in its order
dated 22.12.2020 revived the proceedings arising out of the
Petition under Section 57 of the electricity Act on which the
impugned order was passed by the State Commission and
directed that it be considered and adjudicated upon by by
the Commission on merits in accordance with law. In regard
to the matter for compensation to the Petitioner, the
Commission undertook the proceedings under the UPERC
____________________________________________________________________________________
Appeal No.299 of 2021 Page 5 of 17

Standards of Performance Regulations, 2019 as per which
compensation can only be awarded in case no arrear is due
on the Petitioner. As the petitioner had arrears on account
of final assessment no compensation could be awarded, and
no action could be taken. However, after the settlement of
the final assessment, the electricity connection was restored
by the Respondent hence, no compensation is applicable.
7. On perusal of provisions of the Electricity Act 2003,
Electricity Rules 2005 and Clause 8.1 and 8.2 of the
Electricity Supply Code 2005, the Commission finds that in
case where the authorized officer of the licensee fails to
lodge an FIR within 24 hours or failure to file a case before
the Special Court within 30 days of disconnection, it shall be
construed that the licensee has failed to achieve and
maintain the standards of performance. This conduct of
distribution licensee is non-compliance of the provisions in
the Act, Rules and the Electricity Supply Code 2005.
8. The Commission decides to initiate separate Suo-Moto
proceedings and direct distribution licensees to make
submission in regard to failure to comply with the above
provisions in such cases, as to safeguard the interest of the
consumers as well as distribution licensees. Accordingly, if
necessary, proceedings under Section 142 of the Act may
be initiated by the Commission against the licensees for
non-compliance of above mentioned provisions of Act and
Electricity Supply Code 2005.
____________________________________________________________________________________
Appeal No.299 of 2021 Page 6 of 17

9. Let a proceeding under section 142 of the Electricity Act
be registered.”
8. We have heard Mr. Vatsal Kumar, learned counsel for the appellant,
Mr. Rajiv Srivastava, learned counsel for the 1st, 2nd and 3rd respondents and
Mr. C.K. Rai, learned counsel for the 4th respondent. We have also perused
the written submissions filed by the learned counsels.
9. The appellant is claiming compensation from the distribution licensee
i.e. 2nd respondent on account of failure on its part to lodge an FIR with
regards to the incident of theft of electricity within 24 hours of disconnection
and for failure to file a case before the special court within 30 days of
disconnection of electricity to the appellant’s premises. The appellant relied
upon provisions of Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005, clauses
8.1(xi), 8.2(1) and (x) of which are relevant and are extracted hereinbelow: -
“8.1 (a) Procedure to be adopted by licensee for
Inspection, Provisional Assessment Hearing and Final
assessment in case of theft of electricity under section
135 of the Act.
…
(xi) In the matters where prima facie evidence of theft is
found, the authorized officer of the licensee shall lodge an
F.I.R. within 24 hours of disconnection.
____________________________________________________________________________________
Appeal No.299 of 2021 Page 7 of 17

In case where the authorized officer of the licensee
fails to lodge an F.I.R. within 24 hours of disconnection it
shall be construed that the licensee has failed to achieve and
maintain the standards of performance, and the aggrieved
consumer can directly approach the Commission for the
failure of the licensee in discharging its obligation under
Section 57 of the Act.
…
8.2 Procedure for taking cognizance in case of theft of
electricity:
(i) As per the provisions of the Act and in accordance with
the order dated 8.6.2005 of Ministry of Power under
Electricity Rules, 2005 and power to remove difficulties, and
Electricity (Amendment) Act, 2007, the procedure in clause
8.1 above and as provided herein, does not absolve the
authorized officer of the licensee or supplier, from lodging
the complaint in a police station within 24 hours from the time
of disconnection and filing a case before the Special Court,
within 30 days from the date of disconnection.
On failure of file a case before the Special Court within
30 days of disconnection, it shall be construed that the
licensee has failed to achieve and maintain the standards of
performance, and the aggrieved consumer can directly
approach the Commission for the failure of licensee in
discharging its obligation under Section 57 of the Act, and
____________________________________________________________________________________
Appeal No.299 of 2021 Page 8 of 17

the authorized officer of licensee or supplier shall restore
supply on interim payment of assessed amount, calculated
at 1.0 times of existing tariff, less payment already made by
consumer for the period of assessment within 48 hours of
such deposit or payment. The Authorized Officer shall
subsequently take action for filing the case before the
Special Court.
…
(x) Cognizance of the offence –
(a) A Complaint in writing relating to the commission of such
offence shall be lodged against the consumer or person by
the Appropriate Government or the Appropriate Commission
or any of their authorized officers in this regard or a Chief
Electrical Inspector or an Electrical Inspector or an
authorized officer of Licensee or a Generating Company, as
the case may be, within 24 hours of disconnection, in the
Police Station of that area having Jurisdiction.
(b) The police shall investigate the matter in accordance with
the general law applicable to the investigation of any
offence. For the purposes of investigation of the offence
under the Act or this Code, the police shall have all the
powers as available under the Crpc 1973.
(c) The police shall, after investigation, forward the report
along with the F.I.R. lodged under sub-clause (a) above to
the Court for trial under the Act, i.e. a Special Court, or in
absence of a Special Court, any other Court.
____________________________________________________________________________________
Appeal No.299 of 2021 Page 9 of 17

Provided that, the Court may also take cognizance of an
offence punishable under this Act, upon a report of a
police officer filed under Section 173 of the Code of
Criminal Procedure, 1973.
(d) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-clauses (a),
(b) and (c) above, the complaint for taking cognizance of an
offence punishable under the Act, may also be filed by the
Appropriate Government or the Appropriate Commission or
any of their officer authorized by them or a Chief Electrical
Inspector or an Electrical Inspector or an authorized officer
of Licensee or a Generating Company, as the case may be
directly in the appropriate Court.
(e) Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of
Criminal Procedure, 1973, every Special Court, or in
absence of Special Court, any other Court, shall take
cognizance of an offence referred to in sections 135 to 140
of the Act and Section 150 of the Act, without the accused
being committed to it for trial, and such offence shall be
cognizable and non-bailable.
(f) The cognizance of the offence under the Act, shall not in
any way prejudice the actions under the provision of the
Indian Penal Code.
____________________________________________________________________________________
Appeal No.299 of 2021 Page 10 of 17

(g) The final assessment done by the licensee’s assessing
officer in case of theft, is also subject to adjudication by the
Court.
(h) In case of the decision of the Court that theft is not
established, the charges leveled and assessment made by
the licensee against the consumer or person shall be
withdrawn in writing and the connection shall be restored
through the original meter.”
(Emphasis supplied)
10. Perusal of the above clauses of the Code clearly reveals that the
distribution licensee is duty bound to lodge an FIR with the concerned Police
Station within 24 hours of disconnection of the electricity upon discovering
theft of electricity and subsequently to file a complaint with the concerned
special court within 30 days from the date of disconnection. It is also made
clear in clause 8.1 that in case of default on either count, it shall be treated
as a failure on the part of discom to achieve and maintain the standards of
performance within the meaning of Section 57 of the Electricity Act, 2003,
giving rise to a right to the concerned aggrieved consumer to approach the
appropriate Commission in this regard.
11. Section 57 of the Electricity Act, 2003 becomes material in this
background and is extracted hereinbelow: -
____________________________________________________________________________________
Appeal No.299 of 2021 Page 11 of 17

“Section 57. (Consumer Protection: Standards of
performance of licensee):
(1) The Appropriate Commission may, after consultation
with the licensees and persons likely to be affected, specify
standards of performance of a licensee or a class of
licensees.
(2) If a licensee fails to meet the standards specified under
subsection (1), without prejudice to any penalty which may
be imposed or prosecution be initiated, he shall be liable to
pay such compensation to the person affected as may be
determined by the Appropriate Commission:
Provided that before determination of compensation,
the concerned licensee shall be given a reasonable
opportunity of being heard.
(3) The compensation determined under sub-section (2)
shall be paid by the concerned licensee within ninety days
of such determination.”
12. Sub-section 2 of this statutory provision clearly provides that if the
distribution licensee fails to meet the standards specified under sub-section
1, it shall be liable to pay compensation to the affected person as may be
determined by the appropriate Commission. However, proviso attached to
____________________________________________________________________________________
Appeal No.299 of 2021 Page 12 of 17

clause 7.9 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005, makes the
entitlement of the affected person to compensation subject to the condition
that he has no arrear of electricity dues as on date when the distribution
licensee is stated to have committed failure to meet standards of
performance. The said clause of the Code is extracted hereinbelow: -
“7.9 Compensation
(a) The Licensee shall be liable to pay, to the affected
consumers, compensation as specified in Annexure 7.1 for
Licensees failure to meet the guaranteed standards of
performance. With respect to performance related to
metering and billing, of Annexure 7.1, the liability of
compensation on Licensee shall be effective from the date
of enforcement of the Code. The liability of compensation in
other standards of performance shall be applicable from
such date the Commission may direct by order or notification
issued for the purpose.
(b) Compensation, depending upon the nature of the
complaint, would be released by the concerned Licensee
automatically within 90 days of its, or it would be claimed by
____________________________________________________________________________________
Appeal No.299 of 2021 Page 13 of 17

the consumer from the licensee, as specified in Annexure
7.1.
Provided that:
i. Compensation shall be applicable to only those consumers
who have no arrears on electricity dues, and on conditions,
which are not covered or incidental to factors mentioned in
clause 9.1 of this code.
ii. The licensee shall compensate the person(s) affected not
later than three billing cycles.
iii. No claim for compensation shall be entertained if the
same is filed later than a period of ninety days from the date
of rectification of the deficiency in performance standard.
iv. Such compensation shall be paid or adjusted in the
consumer’s bill issued subsequent to the award of
compensation.
v. Matters related to grievance of any consumer related to
compensation, shall be dealt with in accordance with the
procedure specified in the Business Regulation for filing a
____________________________________________________________________________________
Appeal No.299 of 2021 Page 14 of 17

petition, and the procedure set out in the Consumer
Grievance Redressal Regulations.
vi. The Commission may by a general or special order after
hearing the Licensee and the affected consumer(s) /
consumer groups, release the Licensee from the liability to
compensate the consumers for any default in the
performance of any standard if the Commission is satisfied
that such default is for reasons other than those attributable
to the Licensee and further that the Licensee has otherwise
made efforts to fulfil his obligations.”
(Emphasis supplied)
13. Thus, it is manifest that only those affected persons are entitled to
claim compensation from the distribution licensee for its failure to meet the
standards of performance who are not in arrears of electricity dues. Further,
we also find Regulation 8.1 of UPERC (Standards of Performance)
Regulations, 2019 also relevant in the above context and the same is
reproduced hereinbelow: -
“8. COMPENSATION MECHANISM
8.1 If licensee fails to meet the guaranteed standards of
performance as specified in Schedule-I, licensee shall
____________________________________________________________________________________
Appeal No.299 of 2021 Page 15 of 17

pay compensation to the affected person upon lodging
of a claim for compensation. The compensation to be
paid by the licensee to the affected person is specified
in Schedule-III of these Regulations. If the Consumer
has any arrear, beyond 30 days, on the date of filing the
claim for compensation then no compensation shall be
payable to the consumer.”
(Emphasis supplied)
14. These regulations, even though issued in the year 2019, reiterate what
has been envisaged in clause 7.9 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply
Code, 2005, that the compensation shall be payable to only those consumers
who have no arrears on electricity dues beyond 30 days of the date of filing
of the claim for compensation.
15. In the instant case, the petition claiming compensation under Section
57 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005 was filed by the
appellant on 02.08.2019. The final assessment bill had been issued by the
3rd respondent on 09.04.2019, as already noted. The appellant has,
concededly, not challenged the said bill in any forum/court. The payment
against the said final assessment bill was made by him in the year 2021 in
pursuance to the order dated 27.04.2021 passed by the Commission in the
____________________________________________________________________________________
Appeal No.299 of 2021 Page 16 of 17

petition under reference. Thus, admittedly the appellant was in arrears of
electricity dues in the year 2019, i.e. at the time of filing the claim for
compensation, and therefore, has been rightly held not entitled to
compensation by the Commission in the impugned order.
16. Considering the above discussion, we do not find any error or infirmity
in the impugned order of the Commission. The appeal is devoid of any merit
and is hereby dismissed.
Pronounced in the open court on this the 10th day of September, 2026.
(Ajay Talegaonkar) (Virender Bhat)
Technical Mem ber (Electricity) Judicial Member
